body:
There are two bits to this:

1. A theoretical bug that's existed since 6.6 that would cause the ML memory tracker to become permanently blocked if `onFailure` rather than `onResponse` was called on one of the lower level handlers.  However, there has been no known case of this being suffered by a user, nor has it been seen in any testing prior to 7.3.
2. The fact that in 7.3 we have added a path that is basically guaranteed to trigger the bug, rendering ML completely non-operational.

So it is the combination that makes this a blocker for 7.3.0.

I will fix it in two stages:

1. A fix to the problem of `onFailure` completely blocking up the ML memory tracker.  I'll backport this to 6.8 as theoretically it could be a problem in this version if some really obscure problem happens and it would be difficult to diagnose if a user reported it - the bug report would basically be "ML doesn't work at all", and that's time-consuming to tie down to a particular root cause.
2. An extra check in 7.3.0 and above that prevents the node assignment of data frame analytics jobs at node startup from triggering a failure of the ML memory tracker.  Even when the ML memory tracker recovers from failures it's best to avoid the log spam and confusion they'll cause.

issue.title: [ML] Fix ML memory tracker lockup when inner step fails

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When the ML memory tracker is refreshed and a refresh is
already in progress the idea is that the second and
subsequent refresh requests receive the same response as
the currently in progress refresh.

There was a bug that if a refresh failed then the ML
memory tracker's view of whether a refresh was in progress
was not reset, leading to every subsequent request being
registered to receive a response that would never come.

This change makes the ML memory tracker pass on failures
as well as successes to all interested parties and reset
the list of interested parties so that further refresh
attempts are possible after either a success or failure.

This fixes problem 1 of #44156

issue.title: [ML] Wait for .ml-config primary before assigning persistent tasks

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Now that ML job configs are stored in an index rather than
cluster state, availability of the .ml-config index is very
important to the operation of ML.  When a cluster starts up
the ML persistent tasks will be considered for node
assignment very early on.  It is best in this case if
assignment is deferred until after the .ml-config index is
available.

The introduction of data frame analytics jobs has made this
problem worse, because anomaly detection jobs already waited
for the primary shards of the .ml-state, .ml-anomalies-shared
and .ml-meta indices to be available before doing node
assignment, and by coincidence this would probably lead to
the primary shards of .ml-config also being searchable.  But
data frame analytics jobs had no other index checks prior to
this change.  This is why I propose to only apply this fix to 7.3
and above.

This fixes problem 2 of #44156
